notices.title: Eagle Point - Delaware River/General/Bridges/Maintenance
notices.description:
General/Bridges/Maintenance

From: 2026-01-14 To: 2026-11-30

Location:
40-05-33.068N/074-54-50.440W

Bridge Name: Railroad Bridge
Mariners are advised that maintenance work will be conducted on the Neshaminy Creek Amtrak Railroad Bridge over Neshaminy Creek, approximately 1.5 miles north of the inlet with the Delaware River, from January 19, 2026, to November 30, 2026. Temporary scaffolding will be installed along the bridge fascia and underneath the superstructure, reducing vertical clearance by approximately 4 feet and horizontal clearance by approximately 4 feet on either side. A rescue boat will be on site for emergency use, and ground equipment will include a skid steer, scissor lift, and mini excavator. All work will primarily occur Monday through Thursday, between 6:00 AM to 3:00 PM, with occasional weekend and overnight work as required. The contractor and rescue boat will monitor VHF-FM Channel 13 during work hours. Mariners should adjust their transit plans accordingly and exercise caution when transiting the area. MSI #  35194.

notices.description:
General/Bridges/Temp Deviation

From: 2026-07-20 To: 2027-01-16

Location:
39-21-13.176N/074-27-24.084W

Bridge Name: United States 40-322 Bridge

NJICW - Inside Thorofare

Mariners are advised that the highway drawbridge United States 40-322 (Albany Avenue) Bridge across New Jersey Intracoastal Waterway, Inside Thorofare, mile 70.0, at Atlantic City, NJ, will be maintained in the closed-to-navigation position to facilitate the 16th Annual Atlantic City Triathlon. The bridge will remain in the closed position from 6 a.m. through 12 p.m. on Sunday, August 9, 2026. The bridge will be able to open for emergencies, if at least 30 minutes notice is given. At all other times, the drawbridge will operate in accordance with the operating regulations set out in Title 33 Code of Federal Regulations Part 117.733(h). Mariners should adjust their transits accordingly and should use caution when transiting the area.

notices.title: Cape May Inlet - New Jersey Intracoastal Waterway/General/Bridges/Maintenance
notices.description:
General/Bridges/Maintenance

From: 2026-08-31 To: 2027-04-05

Location:
38-59-27.888N/074-50-00.204W

Bridge Name: 47 State Route Bridge
Mariners are advised that an engineering firm, on behalf of New Jersey Department of Transportation, will be performing maintenance on the highway drawbridge 47 State Route (George Redding) Bridge, across the New Jersey Intracoastal Waterway (NJICW), Grassy Sound Channel, mile 108.9, at Wildwood, NJ. The maintenance will be conducted from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m.; Monday-Friday; from September 14, 2026, through March 31, 2027.  A 40-foot work barge and a tugboat will be located in and around the vicinity of the bridge. During the work hours, the work barge will be located within the entirety of the navigation channel of the bridge to provide access for structural steel repairs to the bascule span. Vessels may safely transit through the bridge, if at least a one-hour prior notice is given to the project foreman. Maintenance personnel, equipment and vessels will relocate from the moveable span and navigable channel, upon request. Work vessels may be reached on VHF-FM channel 13 and 16. The project foreman can be reached at (609) 579-8147. Mariners should use extreme caution navigating through the area.

During the maintenance period, the bridge will be maintained in the closed-to-navigation position to perform structural steel repairs to the bridge bascule span. The bridge will remain in the closed-to-navigation position from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., Monday through Thursday, and from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Friday, from November 30, 2026, through January 22, 2027. The bridge will not be able to open for emergencies. There is no immediate alternative route for vessels unable to pass through the bridge in the closed position. Vessels able to pass through the bridge in the closed position may do so at any time. At all other times, the drawbridge will operate in accordance with the operating regulations set out in Title 33 Code of Federal Regulations Part 117.5. Mariners should adjust their transits accordingly and should use caution when transiting the area.
MSI #52664
